feed.title: [BIP Proposal] BIP324 One-Byte Message Type ID Alias Assignment

entry.title: [BIP Proposal] BIP324 One-Byte Message Type ID Alias Assignment
entry.summary:
The discussion of bandwidth savings in various scenarios reveals significant variations based on the types of messages transmitted over a network connection. For extremely small messages, such as PING/PONG, the savings can be quite substantial, amounting to approximately 66% of the total bandwidth used. This is due to the relative size of the bandwidth saving compared to the small message size. However, for more typical network traffic consisting of INV/GETDATA/TX messages, the expected bandwidth saving drops to about 5%. This reduction reflects the larger size of these messages compared to PING/PONG.
In contrast, when the network is in -blocksonly mode, where traffic predominantly comprises full 2MB BLOCK messages, the percentage of bandwidth saved is minimal, around 0.0006%. This scenario underscores how the impact of the same absolute bandwidth saving can become negligible when spread across much larger data transfers. It is also important to note that these savings only apply when new message types that lack a pre-existing 1-byte identifier are introduced. As long as the existing messages with 1-byte identifiers dominate the traffic, no actual bandwidth saving is realized.
This analysis emphasizes the need to consider both the absolute and relative impacts of optimizations in different operating contexts of network communications within the Bitcoin development community.
